title: Biondi and Malanga's 2022 SAR claim of eight cylindrical structures beneath Giza

tellings.quote: These fascinating open questions, how and why the pyramids got built, became infinitely weirder in 2022. That's when a small team of researchers, led by Italian radar specialist Filippo Biondi and his engineering colleague Corrado Malanga, made one of the boldest claims in the last century involving ancient archaeology.

tellings.difference: Gives the structures as 20 m wide and places them under the Khafre pyramid specifically.
tellings.link_reason: Same claim by Biondi's team that SAR scans show eight hollow cylindrical structures beneath the Khafre pyramid at Giza.

as_told.title: Biondi SAR scans show hollow tubular structures under Khafre pyramid

plain: In 2022, the Italian radar specialist Filippo Biondi and his engineering colleague Corrado Malanga said that satellite radar scans showed eight hollow tube-shaped structures, about 20 meters wide, deep beneath the Khafre pyramid, the second of the great pyramids at Giza in Egypt. Michels tells this himself, calling it "one of the boldest claims in the last century" in ancient archaeology, and in a later episode gives the size and the pyramid. If it held up, it would make the questions of how and why the pyramids were built far stranger.
